hints: No two queens share a row, so each row holds exactly one. What does that make the search?
A choice of column per row - one queen placed at a time, row by row, and the search is over columns rather than over squares.
Before placing a queen, check it against the queens already placed: same column, or same diagonal. Reject there, and the branch is never explored.
The two diagonals through a square are identified by `row + column` and `row - column`. Keeping a set of the used columns and of the used diagonals makes each check O(1).
